text:
sasha: I want to start a short thread on untangling the orchestration plane long-term. Goal: reduce blast radius, pay down tech debt, and make routing/policy changes independently. rough idea below — looking for pushback and migration concerns.

kevin: high-level sounds promising. can you sketch the split you have in mind? where are the hard state boundaries?

sasha: thinking three surface-level components: 1) API Orchestrator (control APIs, rollouts, auth), 2) Conductor (policy store, rollout logic, experiments), 3) Runtime Proxy (latency-sensitive request routing & KV-cache hooks). keep data stores separate or read-only shared during migration.

priya: +1 on separation. migration question: do we plan a big cutover or dual-run? we still have session indices in etcd and some hot pointers in redis.

jordan: prefer phased dual-run. sequence: proxy shim -> move read traffic -> migrate writes -> cutover. each step feature-flagged. minimizes downtime.

mina: observability checklist: trace-id passthrough across components, per-request cost tags, and span-level routing tags so perf shows which component is hot. also make sure sampling doesn't drop canary traces.

kevin: main tradeoff is complexity vs speed of iteration. if we split stores, migrations become trickier (replay needed). single-store keeps consistency but preserves coupling. thoughts on eventual consistency SLA?

priya: proposal: keep single source for authoritative state during migration, use append-only event log for new writes and replay into new store. reads can be feature-flagged to v2 once replay lag under threshold. avoids risky backfill.

sasha: adding a compatibility shim idea: proxy inspects header X-ORCH-VERSION; if absent -> route to v1; if present -> v2. shim returns an alpha header so we can measure usage. cheap and rollback friendly.

kevin: important: proxy must be resilient to mixed-version responses. add a fallback path when v2 returns 5xx and circuit-breaker opens.

jordan: timeline guesstimate: prototype proxy shim (1 sprint), build conductor + policy store (2 sprints), canary in one region + perf tuning (1 sprint), total ~4 sprints to usable canary. assumes no major data migration surprises.

mina: security item: conductor will hold rollout configs that might reference customer ids. coordinate with security for KMS access and audit logs.

priya: test plan: perf harness with synthetic request shapes (short/long contexts), unit of work: ensure KV-cache hit/miss rates don't regress. add regression alert on tail latency and token-cost.

infra-bot: infra-bot: created a runbook stub -> https://intra.redwood/ops/runbooks/orch-untangle (fill in canary gating steps).

kevin: i'll draft a sequencing doc and include rollback criteria (error increase, tail latency > x, cost delta > y). pinging @sasha for acceptance criteria.

sasha: yes please. I'll open an RFC follow-up doc with risks/cost estimate and tech-debt paydown mapping. plan to tag it `orchestration-debt` so it shows on the quarterly paydown board.

priya: one more: add a migration monitor that shows event-log lag and last-successful-replay timestamp. low-effort but high-value.

jordan: agree. also add contract tests that run against both v1 and v2 during canary. they should be part of our CI gating for canary rollouts.

mina: i'll coordinate with observability to add dashboard templates and example queries.

sasha: thanks all. i'll draft the RFC follow-up and link it here when ready. for now i've opened a placeholder doc: https://intra.redwood/docs/orch-untangle-playbook (WIP). :thumbsup:
